problem: If $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ with characteristic polynomial $p(x)={x}^{2}+3x-2,$ then ${A}^{4}=$

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(\lambda ) & =\text{det}(A-\lambda I) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 12 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| \\  & =(4-\lambda )(-4-\lambda ) \\  & ={\lambda }^{2}-16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's divide $f(x)$ by $p(x)$ using long division:

|  | $\,\,{x}^{19}$ |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}^{2}-16\,$ | $\,\enclose{longdiv}{{x}^{21}\,-\,16{x}^{19}\,+\,6x\,\,-\,\,3}$ |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  | ${x}^{21}$ | $-$ | $16{x}^{19}$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  | $6x$ | $-$ | $3$ |

Therefore, we can write $f(x)$ as 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =q(x)p(x)+r(x) \\  & =q(x)p(x)+(6x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

where $q(x)={x}^{19}.$ Replacing $x$ with $A,$ we have

$$
f(A)=q(A)p(A)+(6A-3I).
$$

According to the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we have $p(A)=O.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & =q(A)p(A)+(6A-3I) \\  & =q(A)\cdot O+(6A-3I) \\  & =6A-3I \\  & =6[\begin{aligned}4 & 12 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24 & 72 \\ 0 & -24\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}21 & 72 \\ 0 & -27\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
